newsitem.title: GREECE: Salomon bullish on OTE, Telecom Italia.
newsitem.headline: Salomon bullish on OTE, Telecom Italia.

text.p: Greece's OTE telecom and Telecom Italia are the only buy recommendations among the national operators in Europe, according to research by Salomon Brothers.
"Telecom Italia is just plain cheap on cash flow valuation and OTE is by far the strongest cash flow growth story in Europe," Salomon said in its March European telecommunications research report.
It said worlwide liberalisation measures and market forces were breaking up cosy monopolies and, for investors, were having a profound effect on the outlook for quoted telecoms companies in Europe.
The research foresaw a period of major uncertainty and higher specific investment risk.

"For the most part, Europe's national operators have managed to disguise the growing pressure on fixed line revenues by returning significant cellular growth and by generating free cash flow to pay down debt. This scenario will not last," it said.
The combination of significant price cutting combined with market share loss means national operators need to drive substantially more volume through their networks just to stand still.
Most markets will not be fully liberalised until the start of 1998 and the major impact of competition has yet to be seen.
With the exception of Greece's OTE and Telecom Italia, Salomon opted for an underweight stance on Europe's telecoms as a whole.

"OTE is unique among European operators in that a large percentage of its revenue growth is being derived from digitisation of the local analogue network where charging by length of call has not been technically possible," it said.
